reflection.text:
The high-dose phenotype was real and replicated: 0.6 uM showed enlarged cells with frac_large_nucleus z=+10.0, while both 6 uM replicates showed small rounded cells with frac_mitotic_like z=+12.1 and +20.8, reduced area and solidity, and dose-dependent rise in frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.95. I correctly tracked the biphasic enlargement-to-rounding transition and noted weak multinucleation rho=+0.32, but forced this generic antimitotic-like rounding into the closest atlas classes.

That forcing was the error. The reference comparison never contained Cholesterol-lowering/HMG-CoA reductase inhibition: NSC voted Actin disruptors 2/4 but k-neighbours actually favoured Eg5 inhibitors 5/10 over Actin 3/10, and the first microscopist listed Eg5, Aurora and Microtubule destabilizers. I over-weighted the second 2 uM actin-only call and act_std/act_glcm_contrast rho=+0.95 while ignoring that tub_glcm_contrast also rose rho=+0.95, indicating non-specific cytoskeletal condensation rather than actin-specific stress-fibre loss.

Acquisition compounded it: I sampled only 0.6, 2 and 6 uM where toxicity saturates, never testing the 0.006-0.2 uM range where a statin-specific phenotype might separate from mitotic arrest, and pursued no orthogonal rescue. The review correctly flagged lack of Eg5/Aurora discrimination, but I increased Actin disruptors from 0.55 to 0.62 instead of holding uncertainty for an out-of-set mechanism.
what_was_right: Detected reproducible dose transition from enlarged cells at 0.6 uM (frac_large_nucleus z=+10.0, area z=+5.0) to small rounded mitotic-like cells at 6 uM in two replicates (frac_mitotic_like z=+12.1 and +20.8)
Showed frac_mitotic_like rose dose-dependently rho=+0.95 while frac_multinucleate_proxy was weak rho=+0.32, correctly keeping Aurora vs Eg5 vs actin ambiguity
Recorded lower density vs DMSO and persistent Eg5 k-neighbour majority plus rising tubulin contrast, which signalled a generic rounding/cytokinesis defect rather than a clean actin call
what_was_wrong: Concluded Actin disruptors at p=0.55 then p=0.62 despite reviewer request_experiment warning that Eg5/Aurora were not discriminated
Over-weighted NSC 2/4 vote and second 2 uM actin-only describe_phenotype while discounting first phenotype listing Eg5/Aurora/Microtubule destabilizers and k-neighbour Eg5 5/10 majority
Interpreted act_std and act_glcm_contrast rho=+0.95 as actin-specific while ignoring tub_glcm_contrast rho=+0.95 and cell_area shrinkage, which indicated non-specific mitotic rounding

Never considered a truth outside the hypothesis/atlas set; lookup later confirmed simvastatin HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor, and sampling omitted low doses 0.006-0.2 uM and any mevalonate-rescue orthogonal test
reflection.next_experiment: Low-dose simvastatin dose-response (0.006-0.6 uM) with vs without mevalonate rescue, compared side-by-side to latrunculin B (actin) and Eg5 inhibitor controls, read out by phospho-histone H3, quantitative F-actin/tubulin texture, filipin cholesterol staining and cell viability with washout to test reversibility.

- after step 18: Actin disruptors 0.62, Eg5 inhibitors 0.15, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.10, Protein degradation 0.07, Microtubule destabilizers 0.06

## Conclusion 1

**Actin disruptors** (stated probability 0.55); key evidence e3, e7, e8, e9.

Why: Replicated high-dose profile and NSC vote support leading class; no consistent alternative across doses.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Phospho-histone H3 plus quantitative filamentous-actin imaging dose-response versus reference compounds of the leading and runner-up antimitotic classes, with washout to test reversibility of rounding and mitotic arrest.

## Conclusion 2

**Actin disruptors** (stated probability 0.62); key evidence e3, e7, e8, e14, e15, e16.

Why: 2uM re-exam sole actin call discriminates Eg5/Aurora; uncertainty: Eg5 neighbours persist, tubulin contrast also rises, clustering vs true multinucleation unresolved.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Phospho-histone H3 plus quantitative filamentous-actin imaging dose-response versus reference compounds of the leading and runner-up antimitotic classes, with washout to test reversibility.

## PI review

Verdict: request experiment.

Top call not yet discriminated from Eg5/Aurora. Do not approve at 0.55.

Requested: describe_phenotype on 2 µM single well (dose index 5, rep 1): test F-actin stress-fibre loss/puncta in interphase cells and true multinucleation vs condensed mitotic cells.

## Unblinding

Compound: **simvastatin** (PubChem CID [54454](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/54454))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Actin disruptors**, BBBC021 annotates **Cholesterol-lowering**.

## Reflection

The high-dose phenotype was real and replicated: 0.6 uM showed enlarged cells with frac_large_nucleus z=+10.0, while both 6 uM replicates showed small rounded cells with frac_mitotic_like z=+12.1 and +20.8, reduced area and solidity, and dose-dependent rise in frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.95. I correctly tracked the biphasic enlargement-to-rounding transition and noted weak multinucleation rho=+0.32, but forced this generic antimitotic-like rounding into the closest atlas classes.

That forcing was the error. The reference comparison never contained Cholesterol-lowering/HMG-CoA reductase inhibition: NSC voted Actin disruptors 2/4 but k-neighbours actually favoured Eg5 inhibitors 5/10 over Actin 3/10, and the first microscopist listed Eg5, Aurora and Microtubule destabilizers. I over-weighted the second 2 uM actin-only call and act_std/act_glcm_contrast rho=+0.95 while ignoring that tub_glcm_contrast also rose rho=+0.95, indicating non-specific cytoskeletal condensation rather than actin-specific stress-fibre loss.

Acquisition compounded it: I sampled only 0.6, 2 and 6 uM where toxicity saturates, never testing the 0.006-0.2 uM range where a statin-specific phenotype might separate from mitotic arrest, and pursued no orthogonal rescue. The review correctly flagged lack of Eg5/Aurora discrimination, but I increased Actin disruptors from 0.55 to 0.62 instead of holding uncertainty for an out-of-set mechanism.

What was right:
- Detected reproducible dose transition from enlarged cells at 0.6 uM (frac_large_nucleus z=+10.0, area z=+5.0) to small rounded mitotic-like cells at 6 uM in two replicates (frac_mitotic_like z=+12.1 and +20.8)
- Showed frac_mitotic_like rose dose-dependently rho=+0.95 while frac_multinucleate_proxy was weak rho=+0.32, correctly keeping Aurora vs Eg5 vs actin ambiguity
- Recorded lower density vs DMSO and persistent Eg5 k-neighbour majority plus rising tubulin contrast, which signalled a generic rounding/cytokinesis defect rather than a clean actin call

What was wrong or missed:
- Concluded Actin disruptors at p=0.55 then p=0.62 despite reviewer request_experiment warning that Eg5/Aurora were not discriminated
- Over-weighted NSC 2/4 vote and second 2 uM actin-only describe_phenotype while discounting first phenotype listing Eg5/Aurora/Microtubule destabilizers and k-neighbour Eg5 5/10 majority
- Interpreted act_std and act_glcm_contrast rho=+0.95 as actin-specific while ignoring tub_glcm_contrast rho=+0.95 and cell_area shrinkage, which indicated non-specific mitotic rounding
- Never considered a truth outside the hypothesis/atlas set; lookup later confirmed simvastatin HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor, and sampling omitted low doses 0.006-0.2 uM and any mevalonate-rescue orthogonal test

Proposed next experiment: Low-dose simvastatin dose-response (0.006-0.6 uM) with vs without mevalonate rescue, compared side-by-side to latrunculin B (actin) and Eg5 inhibitor controls, read out by phospho-histone H3, quantitative F-actin/tubulin texture, filipin cholesterol staining and cell viability with washout to test reversibility.
